title: Is Dharoks Effective at Nightmare Zone? (Yes and No)
summary: Gnomonkey explains when Dharok's set is the best DPS option at Nightmare Zone: with high combat stats and Hitpoints it beats everything but a charged scythe, while at lower stats a whip setup has more DPS. He then walks through gear, inventory, dream settings, RuneLite notifications and a 50-second interval timer, reaching about 160k XP an hour.

outline.text: Intro to Nightmare Zone and Dharoking
Overview: how Dharok scales with Hitpoints and DPS comparisons
Setup: gear and special attack weapon
The 50-second interval timer and rapid heal flicking

claims.text: Most equipment sets' DPS scale only with Strength and Attack, but Dharok's also scales heavily with Hitpoints level, each level being about a 1% DPS increase.
Having maxed combat with 70 Hitpoints versus maxed combat with 99 Hitpoints is a 35% DPS difference with Dharok's.

Because of how slowly the axe swings, with base 70 combat stats a Proselyte-and-whip setup gives better DPS than Dharok's; Dharok's begins to beat a whip setup at about 85 base combat stats and Hitpoints.
With high melee stats and Hitpoints or maxed combat, a whip setup gives about 20% less DPS than Dharok's, and a Ghrazi rapier with best-in-slot melee gear is still about 5% worse than Dharok's.
The only setup that beats Dharok's DPS-wise is a charged scythe at about 10% more DPS; an uncharged scythe is still worse.
Gnomonkey says that for the 99.99% of players who cannot spend 1.4 million an hour on a scythe at NMZ, Dharok's is probably going to stay the best method.

The only downside of Dharok's is that it is less AFK than a Proselyte whip setup, but it gives significantly better XP an hour and costs much less over time because the player does not pray Protect from Melee.
Nightmare Zone is located just outside Yanille and lets players refight quest bosses; Gnomonkey says it is known as the best place to train combat, to the point some call it overpowered.

Gnomonkey picks a customizable Hard rumble dream, because Hard mode doubles the bosses' offensive stats and health but not their defence, and since the player's health is 1 it only increases XP an hour and points an hour.
Gnomonkey's chosen bosses are Count Draynor, Sand Snake, Moss Guardian, Agrith-Na-Na and the Ice Troll King, which give a bonus experience multiplier and inflict no status effects.
The Power Surge power-up gives 45 seconds of infinite special attack, dramatically increasing damage and XP an hour; Gnomonkey grabs it and pulls out his spec weapon.
Gnomonkey considers Power Surge the only power-up worth worrying about, since the others do not improve XP and just kill or damage monsters faster.

With this setup Gnomonkey gets on average 160k XP an hour depending on Power Surge spawns, and 270k points per hour; the hurt boxes (rewards) pay for the entrance fee and Dharok's repairs, leaving only the cost of prayer potions.

Gnomonkey assumes basic gear: Dharok's, a blessing, an imbued Berserker ring and a fire cape; an amulet of torture gives 2% more DPS than a fury, Ferocious gloves 2% more than Barrows gloves, and Primordial boots a fraction of a percent (Dragon boots are acceptable).
Gnomonkey's spec weapon is dragon claws, which he bought with 50 mil he had around and says are just slightly better than a granite maul with a handle; a granite maul is totally fine.

With Dragon Slayer II completed, a locator orb is the most efficient way to damage yourself outside the Wilderness, hitting for 10 each click, unlike the dwarven rock cake whose damage scales down as health lowers; neither can kill you.
Inventory is 12 doses of overload, 24 doses of absorption, a holy wrench and the rest prayer potions; Gnomonkey says this is the perfect ratio to last one hour.

Gnomonkey brings extra absorptions in case the overload runs out and he gets hit hard, and has run out of absorptions before prayer potions; more locator orbs can be obtained from Ava at Draynor Manor.

On entering, Gnomonkey sips overload (hits for 50 HP), drinks absorption to 200 and no higher, reduces health to 1, turns on Piety, auto-retaliate and the interval timer, and sits on the sides to reduce being hit by multiple enemies.
Gnomonkey recommends enabling RuneLite game notifications, which play a tone when something happens like a power surge spawning or low prayer, so the player can keep their eyes off the screen longer.

In the Nightmare Zone plugin Gnomonkey checks only power surge power-ups, as they are the only ones that boost XP an hour, and sets notifications for overload about to run out and absorption below 50.

A 50-second interval timer beeps every 50 seconds so the player can flick rapid heal on and off, resetting the health restore timer to one minute; this keeps health at 1 without the orb, improving DPS and XP an hour and saving absorption potions.
